services.name: Abhyanga
services.short_desc: A warm-oil, full-body massage with flowing, rhythmic strokes.
services.long_desc: This placeholder ritual uses warm herbal oils selected for your preferences. Gentle, coordinated strokes support relaxation and a feeling of grounding. Your practitioner discusses pressure and sensitivities before the session. It is a wellness experience, not a medical treatment.

services.name: Shirodhara
services.short_desc: A steady stream of warm oil over the forehead invites quiet stillness.
services.long_desc: Shirodhara is traditionally used as a calming wellness practice. A practitioner gently pours warm oil across the forehead while you rest comfortably. The experience supports time away from everyday stimulation. Suitability and comfort are discussed before beginning.

services.name: Panchakarma Detox
services.short_desc: A spa-level wellness ritual inspired by traditional Ayurvedic practices.
services.long_desc: This introductory experience combines gentle warmth, massage and rest. It traditionally supports a considered self-care routine. The spa offering does not include medical cleansing procedures or guaranteed detoxification. A qualified clinician should advise on clinical Panchakarma.

services.name: Udvartana
services.short_desc: An invigorating herbal-powder massage with upward, energising strokes.
services.long_desc: A blend of finely prepared herbs is used in a rhythmic dry massage. The ritual supports gentle exfoliation and skin conditioning. Your practitioner adapts pressure to your comfort and checks for sensitivities. Results vary and no body-shape changes are promised.

services.name: Kati Basti
services.short_desc: Localised warmth and warm oil are traditionally used for lower-back comfort.
services.long_desc: A comfortable oil reservoir is created over the lower back using a dough boundary. Warm oil is maintained for a short, supervised period. This wellness ritual supports relaxation around the lower back. Persistent or severe pain needs assessment by a qualified healthcare professional.

services.name: Pizhichil
services.short_desc: Continuous warm oil and gentle massage create a deeply restful ritual.
services.long_desc: Pizhichil combines warm oil application with coordinated massage. Traditionally used as a nourishing wellness practice, it encourages comfort and rest. Your practitioner explains each step and adjusts temperature carefully. It is not a substitute for care for joint or muscle conditions.

services.name: Netra Tarpana
services.short_desc: A traditional eye-area wellness ritual centred on rest and stillness.
services.long_desc: This placeholder offering is a supervised, non-invasive eye-area comfort ritual. It encourages a quiet break from screens and everyday visual demands. No eye conditions are treated or diagnosed. Clinical eye procedures require an appropriately qualified practitioner and separate assessment.

services.name: Nasya
services.short_desc: A gentle facial and steam experience inspired by the tradition of Nasya.
services.long_desc: This spa adaptation combines a gentle facial massage with comfortable external steam. It is traditionally associated with a feeling of freshness in the head and neck area. No nasal medication is administered in this wellness offering. Ask a clinician about clinical Nasya or persistent symptoms.

services.name: Mukha Lepa Herbal Facial
services.short_desc: A cooling herbal facial tailored to your skin preferences.
services.long_desc: Gentle cleansing is followed by a herbal mask and a relaxed facial massage. Ingredients are discussed in advance and a patch test may be recommended. The ritual supports skin conditioning and a refreshed appearance. It does not diagnose or treat skin disease.
services.image_alt: Illustrative imagery for Mukha Lepa Herbal Facial

services.name: Garbhini Care
services.short_desc: A gentle, position-adapted massage for expectant guests with clinical clearance.
services.long_desc: This placeholder ritual is adapted for comfort during pregnancy. Written clearance from the guest’s maternity clinician and a trained prenatal practitioner are required. Positioning and pressure are adjusted throughout the session. It does not replace antenatal care or treat pregnancy complications.

services.name: Ayurvedic Consultation
services.short_desc: A wellness conversation about your routines, preferences and goals.
services.long_desc: A practitioner listens to your daily routine and self-care goals. The discussion explores traditional Ayurvedic concepts and suitable spa experiences. Educational guidance is individualised without promising medical outcomes. Medical diagnosis and medication decisions remain with your healthcare professional.

services.name: Yoga & Meditation
services.short_desc: A gentle movement and guided-breathing session adaptable to experience.
services.long_desc: A practitioner guides comfortable movement, breathing awareness and rest. Options are offered for different mobility levels and experience. The session supports a mindful pause rather than athletic performance. Tell your practitioner about injuries or pregnancy before participating.

faqs.question: What should I expect on my first visit?
faqs.answer: Please arrive 15 minutes early. We will talk through your preferences, sensitivities and comfort before your ritual. Share any medical concerns with your clinician before booking.

faqs.question: Are these rituals medical treatments?
faqs.answer: No. Our spa experiences support general wellness and do not replace medical diagnosis or treatment. Speak with a qualified clinician about health concerns.

faqs.question: Can I book during pregnancy?
faqs.answer: Please tell us when booking. Garbhini Care requires clearance from your maternity clinician and an appropriately trained practitioner. Your safety comes first.

faqs.question: How do I choose a service?
faqs.answer: Explore the ritual descriptions, try our educational dosha quiz, or choose a wellness consultation. Your practitioner can help you understand the spa options.

faqs.question: What should I bring?
faqs.answer: Comfortable clothing and anything that helps you feel at ease. Please let us know about allergies, sensitivities or accessibility needs in your booking notes.

faqs.question: What if I need to reschedule?
faqs.answer: Please contact the studio as soon as your plans change. The final cancellation and rescheduling policy will be provided by the studio before launch.

blog_posts.title: Making room for a slower morning
blog_posts.excerpt: Small, sustainable ideas for a more mindful start. No perfect routine required.
blog_posts.body:
Before the day asks anything of you, take a moment to notice how you feel. Open a curtain. Drink a glass of water. Let your shoulders settle.

Begin with something small

A few comfortable stretches or a quiet cup of herbal tea can become a gentle cue to slow down. There is no single routine that suits everyone.

Choose something enjoyable and realistic. Consistent rest and gentle routines support everyday wellbeing; they do not replace medical care.

blog_posts.title: Understanding the three doshas
blog_posts.excerpt: An introductory, educational guide to Vata, Pitta and Kapha.
blog_posts.body:
Ayurvedic tradition describes three doshas as a framework for understanding individual patterns: Vata, Pitta and Kapha. This is a traditional lens, not a medical diagnosis.

A language for observation

Vata is often associated with movement, Pitta with transformation, and Kapha with stability. Everyone is described as a unique combination.

Our quiz is a simple educational introduction. It cannot determine your health needs or the suitability of a therapy. Discuss persistent symptoms with a qualified clinician.
blog_posts.cover_alt: Illustrative cover for Understanding the three doshas

blog_posts.title: Preparing for your first spa visit
blog_posts.excerpt: A few thoughtful questions to ask before choosing your first ritual.
blog_posts.body:
Your first visit should feel comfortable from the moment you arrive. Allow a little extra time, wear comfortable clothing and bring any questions you have.

Let your practitioner know

Share relevant allergies, sensitivities, pregnancy, medications and access needs. Ask about ingredients, pressure, session length and aftercare before beginning.

Ayurvedic spa therapies support general wellness and do not replace medical treatment. Consult your doctor, especially if pregnant or under treatment.
